cover.title: Three-Party Partnership Proposal: IndiGo Airlines, InterGlobe Hotels and BlueDart
cover.subtitle: Flights, stays and last-mile delivery in one packaged journey
cover.request: Turn that into a client-ready proposal deck: every party, how the collaboration works, the commercial logic, risks and shortcomings, and next steps. Make it descriptive, not a wall of tables.

sections.title: Three-party bundle can pilot without ceding inventory or pricing control

items.text: The bundle packages flights, hotel stays and last-mile delivery into one offer.
Each partner fulfils its own leg under its own terms, with no ceding of inventory or pricing control.
The commercial model must work across three P&Ls, using a packaging fee and attach share.
Operational coupling and peak inventory are the main risks to manage.
A pilot should prove one route pair and one city before any joint entity is discussed.

sections.speakerNotes: This slide frames the proposal: a three-party bundle that sells as one offer but keeps each partner's fulfilment and pricing independent. The pilot scope is one route pair and one city.
sections.takeaway: A pilot can test the bundle without any partner giving up control of its own inventory or pricing.
warnings: No passage cited.
